product_family: AI creative suite for image, video, and 3D generation/editing (Krea app, Krea 2 realtime/native models, upscaling, LoRA fine-tuning) plus a pay-per-use API, a Business/Enterprise tier with contractual data protections, and separately licensed open-weight Krea 2 models distributed on Hugging Face.

certifications.name: SOC 2
certifications.proof_quote: SOC2 Bridge Letter ... Request | Krea operates a continuously monitored and third-party audited security program. This page provides access to trust resources including policies, audits, pentests, and real-time status against security controls.

certifications.name: ISO 27001
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. Krea's own trust center (trust.krea.ai) lists only a SOC2 Bridge Letter, CAIQ v4.0.2, and a 2025 pen test as requestable documents; ISO 27001 is not mentioned anywhere on krea.ai or trust.krea.ai. A third-party research aggregator (Contrary Research) states Krea was 'expected to launch...with compliance credentials including SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001' but this is a forward-looking, unconfirmed third-party statement, not a vendor claim or proof.

certifications.name: GDPR
certifications.proof_quote: GDPR is a regulation, not a certifiable standard. Krea's trust center lists an 'Enterprise Data Processing Addendum (DPA)' available on request and a linked Privacy Policy, but no vendor page publishes GDPR-specific representations such as an EU representative, SCCs, or EU data residency.

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. No mention of HIPAA, PHI, or a Business Associate Agreement anywhere on krea.ai or trust.krea.ai. Product is a general creative/generative-media tool, not marketed for healthcare data.

certifications.name: PCI DSS
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence and likely not applicable directly to Krea: payment processing is delegated to Stripe (listed as a subprocessor: 'Stripe / Payment Processing / Data location: US'), which typically removes Krea itself from PCI DSS scope for card data.

certifications.name: ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management system)
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence. Not mentioned on krea.ai or trust.krea.ai.

certifications.name: CSA STAR
certifications.proof_quote: No CSA STAR registry listing found. Krea's trust center offers a 'CAIQv4.0.2' (CSA Consensus Assessment Initiative Questionnaire) as a requestable 'Security, Privacy, Compliance overview' document, which is a related CSA artifact but is not the same as a published CSA STAR certification/attestation, and no STAR listing is claimed.

certifications.name: FedRAMP
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence; product is a consumer/commercial creative-AI tool with no indication of targeting U.S. federal government customers.

privacy.ai_training_note: Training practice differs by plan tier. The Enterprise page states plainly: 'We never use customer data to train or improve our models, and we never will.' The Pricing page describes the Business plan as including 'data protection and no-training clauses for your content,' implying this is a paid/contractual protection rather than a default. The homepage also lists 'Do not train / Safely generate proprietary data' as a named feature/capability rather than a blanket guarantee, which is consistent with default Free/Basic/Pro usage being eligible for training unless a customer is on a Business/Enterprise agreement with a no-training clause. No single vendor page states an unconditional 'we never train on any user's content' for all tiers.
privacy.data_region: US. Every subprocessor listed on the trust center (AWS, Stripe, GitHub, Grafana, PostHog, Cloudflare, Retool, Linear) shows 'Data location: US'; no EU or other regional hosting option is publicly documented.

top_certs: SOC 2 (bridge letter referenced; full report/type not publicly disclosed, available under NDA)

flags: SOC 2 status is ambiguous on the public trust center: only a 'SOC2 Bridge Letter' is listed as a requestable resource, not the underlying SOC 2 report itself, and Type I vs Type II is never stated publicly. A bridge letter is only issued to organizations that have already completed at least one SOC 2 examination, so this is real (not fabricated) evidence of an underlying audit, but AIFOXX should request the actual report before displaying a firm 'SOC 2 Type II' badge.

A third-party aggregator (Contrary Research) states Krea 'is ISO 27001 compliant' and was 'expected to launch... with SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001.' This is speculative, forward-looking, third-party language that is not confirmed on any krea.ai or trust.krea.ai page.

The AI training posture varies by plan tier: the Enterprise page's blanket 'we never train on customer data' statement applies to Enterprise (and, per pricing, Business) plans, while Free/Basic/Pro plans have no equivalent public no-training guarantee; 'Do not train' is marketed as a differentiated feature on paid tiers.
No HIPAA, PCI DSS, ISO/IEC 42001, CSA STAR, or FedRAMP evidence exists; none of these appear applicable to this product category today.
All subprocessors are US-hosted with no public EU data residency option, which is relevant context for GDPR-sensitive prospective customers even though Krea does offer an Enterprise DPA on request.
